mainTopic: How the מזבח was built without cutting, how דוד and שמואל found the place of the בית המקדש, and the rules of שלמי צבור and אשמות
overview: The גמרא finishes a discussion about how the מזבח was built. Cutting the altar's stones is forbidden, so to leave a section without a יסוד, something was placed under the frame and removed after the mixture hardened. רב כהנא's teaching that the corners of the מזבח were hollow proves this method. The גמרא then tells an אגדה: רבא explains that דוד and שמואל sat in רמה discussing the בית המקדש, 'the beauty of the world.' A פסוק taught them that the מקדש must be on the highest place. From the borders in ספר יהושע they found that this place is in בנימין's portion. They put it a little below the peak, either because of the words 'between his shoulders' or to stay close to the סנהדרין in יהודה. This discovery made דואג האדומי jealous of דוד, and a פסוק in תהלים hints to יהושע and בנימין. Finally, a new משנה lists שלמי צבור and the six kinds of אשם and gives their rules: slaughter in the north, two placements that count as four, and eating in the courtyard by male כהנים until midnight.

steps.title: You cannot cut the altar's stones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the builder cut away part of the poured altar, because the Torah requires 'whole stones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that he cuts it away, it is written 'whole stones'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking how part of the מזבח could be left without a יסוד. It rejects one possible answer: that the builder cut the hardened material away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires the מזבח to be built of 'whole stones' (אבנים שלמות), meaning stones that are not cut. Cutting the hardened mixture after it was poured would break that rule. So the cutting answer cannot be right, and the גמרא needs another explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: cuts, trims away
whole (uncut) stones, required for the מזבח
it is written

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a thought from the previous עמוד, which asked how the corner without a יסוד was made. The words 'if you say' are understood.

phrases.english: [If you say] that he cuts it,
phrases.notes: This carries on from the end of the previous עמוד: suppose he cuts away the part that shouldn't have a base.

phrases.notes: דברים 27:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous עמוד's discussion of how the area without a יסוד was formed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the builder cut away the poured altar material to leave a space without a יסוד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah requires the altar's stones to be whole and uncut, so cutting is not allowed.

steps.title: Place something underneath and remove it
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the builder put an object under the frame and pulled it out after the mixture hardened.
steps.simpleTranslation: He places something under it, and then removes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Nothing was cut; an object held the space open and was taken out later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the empty space came from removing a filler object and not from cutting, the altar stays made of 'whole stones.' The rule is kept and the desired shape is still achieved.

keyTerms.meaning: places, puts down
something, some object
takes, removes

phrases.english: That he places something underneath it,
and removes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical method that avoids the forbidden act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The space without a יסוד must have been made by cutting, which is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: A filler object was placed under the frame and removed after the mixture set, so nothing was cut.

steps.title: Proof from רב כהנא's hollow corners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the method from רב כהנא's teaching that the altar's corners were hollow, which must also have been done without cutting.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say so, how do you explain what רב כהנא said: the stones of the corners were hollow, as it says, 'And they shall be filled like the basin, like the corners of the altar'? There too, the Torah said 'whole stones'! Rather, he placed something underneath and removed it. Here too, he places something underneath and removes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer. רב כהנא already taught that the corners were hollow, and the same 'place and remove' method must explain that too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hollow corners raise the same problem: how do you get a hollow without cutting 'whole stones'? The only answer is to put something inside, pour around it, and remove it. Since that method is accepted for the corners, it works for the area without a יסוד as well.

keyTerms.meaning: the corners (horns) of the מזבח
hollow
a basin used for the blood
the Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The altar's stones could never be cut. Any empty spaces, such as the section without a יסוד or the hollow corners, were made by placing something in the mold and removing it after the material hardened.

steps.title: דוד and שמואל discuss the beauty of the world
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'Naioth in Ramah' means דוד and שמואל sat in רמה and discussed the בית המקדש, 'the beauty of the world.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the verse mean, 'And דוד and שמואל went and sat in Naioth in Ramah'? What does Naioth have to do with Ramah? Rather, they sat in Ramah and were busy with the beauty of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from building the מזבח to an אגדה about the בית המקדש. רבא reads a strange phrase in a פסוק as a hint to the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נויות and רמה seem to be two different places, so the פסוק is puzzling. רבא reads נויות as נויו, 'its beauty': they sat in רמה and discussed the beauty of the world, the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: taught or explained a פסוק
Naioth, a name in the פסוק
Ramah, שמואל's town
the beauty of the world, meaning the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is [the meaning of] that which is written:
"And David and Samuel went
and sat in Naioth in Ramah"?
phrases.notes: שמואל א 19:18–19

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן נוֹיוֹת אֵצֶל רָמָה?
phrases.english: But what does Naioth have to do with Ramah?
Rather, that they were sitting in Ramah
and were occupied with the beauty of the world.
phrases.notes: A play on words: נויות sounds like נויו, 'its beauty.' The beauty of the world is the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, linked to the previous discussion through the theme of the מזבח and the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד and שמואל sat in רמה and discussed the בית המקדש, which is called the beauty of the world.

steps.title: The מקדש must be on the highest place
steps.stepSummary: דוד and שמואל learned from a פסוק that the בית המקדש is higher than all of ארץ ישראל, but they did not know where that spot was.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: It is written, 'And you shall arise and go up to the place.' This teaches that the בית המקדש is higher than all of ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is higher than all lands. They did not know where the place was.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the story of דוד and שמואל. It explains what they were discussing and sets up the next part of the גמרא: how they will find the right place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'arise and go up' show that you must climb to reach the מקדש, so it must stand on the highest point. They knew this rule but did not know which spot was the highest. The next step answers this question.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall go up
high, higher
its place

steps.confusionAlert: 'They did not know' does not end the story. It is the setup for the search that comes next.

phrases.english: They said: It is written:
phrases.notes: 'They' are דוד and שמואל, still sitting in רמה.

phrases.english: "And you shall arise and go up to the place" –
phrases.notes: דברים 17:8

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ גָּבוֹהַּ מִכׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: this teaches that the Temple is higher than all of Eretz Yisrael,
and Eretz Yisrael is higher than all lands.
They did not know where its place was;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what דוד and שמואל were discussing in step 4 and opens the question of where the מקדש belongs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית המקדש must stand on the highest place in ארץ ישראל, but דוד and שמואל did not yet know where that was.

steps.title: Finding the spot from the borders in ספר יהושע
steps.stepSummary: דוד and שמואל check ספר יהושע and see that only בנימין's border goes 'up' and never 'down,' so the highest place must be in בנימין's portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought ספר יהושע. For all the tribes it says 'and the border went down,' 'and the border went up,' 'and the border was drawn.' But for בנימין it only says 'and it went up,' never 'and it went down.' They said: we learn from this that this is the place.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 5 דוד and שמואל did not know where the highest spot was. Now they find the answer by reading the border descriptions in ספר יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other tribe's border goes both up and down. בנימין's border only goes up, which shows it reaches the highest ground. Since the בית המקדש must be the highest place in ארץ ישראל, it belongs in בנימין's portion.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of יהושע, which lists the borders of each tribe
Border
And it went down
And it went up
Learn from this; we can conclude

steps.whyThisMatters: This is how the area of the בית המקדש is first identified: it is in בנימין's portion.

phrases.english: They brought the book of Joshua.
phrases.notes: "They" means דוד and שמואל, who were trying to find the spot in step 5.

phrases.english: Regarding all of the tribes it is written:
"And went down," ("and the border went up"),
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way, the other tribes' borders also go down.

phrases.english: "and the border was drawn";
for the tribe of Benjamin, "and went up" is written,
but "and went down" is not written.
They said: Learn from this:
here is its place.
phrases.notes: "Its place" means the place of the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open question from step 5 about where the highest spot is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The highest spot, and so the place of the בית המקדש, is in בנימין's portion, since only its border goes up and never down.

steps.title: Lowering the site a little below עין עיטם
steps.stepSummary: They planned to build at the highest point, עין עיטם, but decided to place it a little lower because of the פסוק 'and He dwells between his shoulders.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought to build it at עין עיטם, which is high. They said: let us lower it a little, as it is written, 'and He dwells between his shoulders.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that they know the area, דוד and שמואל pick the exact spot. They first choose the very top, עין עיטם, and then move it a bit lower.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain idea was that the highest spot is the best. But the פסוק says the שכינה rests 'between his shoulders,' and shoulders are a bit lower than the head. So the בית המקדש should be slightly below the very peak.

keyTerms.meaning: A high place in בנימין's portion
Which is high
Let us lower it
And He dwells between his shoulders (דברים 33:12)

phrases.english: They thought to build it at Ein Eitam,
which is high;
they said: Let us lower it a little,
as it is written: "And He dwells between his shoulders."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:12, from the ברכה to בנימין. Shoulders sit a bit below the head, so the spot should be a bit below the top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the general area found in step 6 to an exact spot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית המקדש was placed slightly lower than עין עיטם, based on 'between his shoulders.'

steps.title: Second reason: staying close to the סנהדרין in יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Another reason for lowering the site: by tradition the סנהדרין is in יהודה's portion and the שכינה in בנימין's, and a higher site would be too far from יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: we have a tradition that the סנהדרין is in יהודה's portion and the שכינה is in בנימין's portion. If we raise it, they will be too far apart. Better to lower it a little, as it is written, 'and He dwells between his shoulders.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason why they did not build at עין עיטם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the reason was only the פסוק. Here there is a practical reason: the סנהדרין in יהודה's portion must not be too far from the בית המקדש in בנימין's portion. Building lower keeps them close, and the פסוק fits this too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; introduces another explanation
We have a tradition
The high court
The Divine Presence
It will be too far apart

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
we have a tradition that the Sanhedrin is in the portion of Judah
and the Divine Presence is in the portion of Benjamin,
and if we raise it,
it will be too far apart;
phrases.notes: The בית המקדש would be too far from יהודה's portion, where the סנהדרין sits.

phrases.english: it is better that we lower it a bit,
as it is written: "And He dwells between his shoulders."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason for the same decision made in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The site was lowered so the בית המקדש in בנימין's portion would stay close to the סנהדרין in יהודה's portion.

steps.title: דואג האדומי's jealousy over the discovery
steps.stepSummary: Because דוד found the place of the בית המקדש, דואג האדומי became jealous of him, and the גמרא brings פסוקים from תהלים about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of this, דואג האדומי was jealous of דוד, as it says: 'for jealousy for Your house has eaten me up.' And it says: 'ה׳, remember for דוד all his affliction, how he swore to ה׳: I will not come into the tent of my house, I will not give sleep to my eyes or slumber to my eyelids, until I find a place for ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the story by saying that דוד's success in finding the spot made דואג האדומי jealous of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says that jealousy connected to 'Your house,' the בית המקדש, hurt דוד, which the גמרא reads as the jealousy דואג felt toward him. The second פסוק shows how hard דוד worked, refusing to rest until he found 'a place for ה׳.'

keyTerms.meaning: Was jealous
Doeg the Edomite, a leader in שאול's time
Jealousy over Your house
His affliction; his suffering

steps.whatToRemember: דוד and שמואל found the place of the בית המקדש from the borders in ספר יהושע: in בנימין's portion, slightly below the top, close to יהודה. This discovery made דואג jealous of דוד.

phrases.english: And about this matter,
phrases.notes: This matter is דוד and שמואל finding the place of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Doeg the Edomite was jealous of David,
as it is written: "For jealousy for Your house has eaten me up,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 69:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the result of the discovery described in steps 6-8: דואג's jealousy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דואג האדומי was jealous of דוד because דוד found the place of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: אפרתה and the field of the forest point to יהושע and בנימין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the פסוק 'We heard of it in אפרתה, we found it in the field of the forest.' אפרתה hints to יהושע, who came from אפרים. The field of the forest hints to בנימין, who is called a wolf.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Behold, we heard of it in Ephrath; we found it in the field of the forest.' 'In Ephrath' means יהושע, who came from אפרים. 'We found it in the field of the forest' means בנימין, as it says, 'בנימין is a wolf that tears.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads one more פסוק from the same chapter of תהלים. It shows that the פסוק hints to how דוד and שמואל found the place of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 6, דוד and שמואל used ספר יהושע to work out that the highest spot was in בנימין's portion. This פסוק sums up that process in two parts. 'We heard of it in Ephrath' means they learned it from יהושע, a man of אפרים. 'We found it in the field of the forest' means they found it in the land of בנימין, the 'wolf' who lives out in the wild.

keyTerms.meaning: Ephrath; here read as a hint to אֶפְרַיִם, the tribe of יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
The field of the forest, a wild place where animals like wolves live
A wolf that tears its prey; יַעֲקֹב's description of בִּנְיָמִין
Who comes from (a family or tribe)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole story fits together: a פסוק taught that the מקדש is at the highest place, ספר יהושע showed the highest place is in בנימין's portion, and the פסוק in תהלים hints to both יהושע and בנימין.

phrases.english: "Behold, we heard of it in Ephrath;
phrases.notes: תהלים 132:6

phrases.english: we found it in the field of the forest."
"In Ephrath": this is יהושע,
who comes from אפרים.
phrases.notes: This hints back to step 6, where דוד and שמואל used ספר יהושע to find the highest place.

phrases.english: "We found it in the field of the forest": this is בנימין,
as it is written: "Benjamin is a wolf that tears."
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:27. A wolf lives out in the wild field, so 'the field of the forest' hints to בנימין.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִנֵּה שְׁמַעֲנוּהָ בְאֶפְרָתָה מְצָאנוּהָ בִּשְׂדֵה יַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the פסוקים from תהלים brought in step 9 and reads the next פסוק as a hint to the method from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אפרתה hints to יהושע of אפרים, whose book was the source. The field of the forest hints to בנימין, whose portion holds the place of the מקדש.

steps.title: New משנה: communal peace offerings and the six kinds of guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens with communal peace offerings and guilt offerings. It then lists the six kinds of אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Communal peace offerings and guilt offerings. These are the guilt offerings: the אשם for robbery, the אשם for misusing holy property, the אשם for a promised maidservant, the אשם of a נזיר, the אשם of a מצורע, and the doubtful אשם.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here and names which offerings it will discuss. This step sets up the list, and the next step gives their rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה groups שלמי צבור together with all the אשמות because they share the same set of rules. It names each kind of אשם so that none is left out. Each one is brought for a different reason, but they are all treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal peace offerings, brought for the whole people (the two lambs of שָׁבוּעוֹת)
Guilt offering brought by someone who denied owing money and swore falsely
Guilt offering for accidentally using holy property for personal use
A maidservant who has been promised in marriage to a Hebrew slave
The 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned

steps.confusionAlert: Regular שלמים are קדשים קלים and may be eaten anywhere in ירושלים by anyone. שלמי צבור are different: they are קדשי קדשים, which is why they appear here with the אשמות.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The offerings of communal peace offerings and guilt offerings:
These are the guilt offerings:
the guilt offering for robbery, the guilt offering for misuse of holy property,
the guilt offering of a promised maidservant,
the guilt offering of a נזיר, the guilt offering of a מצורע,
and the doubtful guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story is over. A new משנה begins with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's subject is שלמי צבור and all six types of אשם.

steps.title: The rules for slaughtering, blood and eating these offerings
steps.stepSummary: These offerings are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is received in the north. The blood gets two placements that count as four. The meat is eaten in the courtyard by male כהנים, prepared any way, for a day and a night until midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is received in a holy vessel in the north. Their blood needs two placements that are four. They are eaten inside the curtains, by male כהנים, prepared any way, on that day and the following night until midnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the rules for all the offerings it just listed. It covers where they are slaughtered, how the blood is placed, and who may eat them, where and until when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the rules of קדשי קדשים. The slaughter and the receiving of the blood must be done in the northern part of the courtyard. The blood is put on two opposite corners of the מזבח so that it touches all four sides. The meat is eaten only inside the courtyard, only by male כהנים, and only until midnight of the night after the offering was brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The north side of the courtyard, where קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים are slaughtered
A holy service vessel used in the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
Two placements of blood that count as four
Inside the curtains, meaning inside the courtyard (עֲזָרָה)
Until midnight

steps.whatToRemember: שלמי צבור and all six אשמות share the rules of קדשי קדשים: north, two placements that count as four, and eaten in the courtyard by male כהנים until midnight.

phrases.english: Their slaughter is in the north,
and the receiving of their blood in a service vessel is in the north,

phrases.aramaic: וְדָמָן טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: and their blood requires two placements that are four,
phrases.notes: The blood goes on two opposite corners of the מזבח, so it touches all four sides.

phrases.english: and they are eaten inside the curtains,
phrases.notes: 'The curtains' are the walls of the courtyard of the משכן, so this means inside the courtyard.

phrases.english: by male כהנים, prepared in any manner of food,
for the day and the night, until midnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחִיטָתָן בַּצָּפוֹן וְקִיבּוּל דָּמָן בִּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת בַּצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rules for the offerings listed in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These offerings are slaughtered and their blood received in the north, get two placements that are four, and are eaten in the courtyard by male כהנים, prepared any way, until midnight.
